questions.question: She ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular in the present tense takes -s: she goes.

questions.question: The past tense of 'write' is
questions.explanation: 'Wrote' is the simple past; 'written' is the past participle.

questions.question: Neither of the boys ___ present.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'was'.

questions.question: He has lived here ___ 2019.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time; 'for' is used with a period of time.

questions.question: A synonym of 'happy' is
questions.explanation: Joyful means the same as happy; the rest are opposites or unrelated.

questions.question: An antonym of 'ancient' is
questions.explanation: Modern is the opposite of ancient; old, antique and aged are synonyms.

questions.question: 'Benevolent' means
questions.explanation: Benevolent means kind and generous — wishing to do good.

questions.question: 'To bite the dust' means to
questions.explanation: To bite the dust means to fail or suffer defeat.

questions.question: He said, 'I am tired.' In reported speech: He said that he ___ tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the tense shifts one step back: am becomes was.

questions.question: The plural of 'analysis' is
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -sis change to -ses: analysis becomes analyses.

questions.question: Rewrite in the plural: 'The child is playing.'
questions.explanation: child becomes children, and the verb becomes plural: are.

questions.question: Give the noun form of 'decide'.
questions.explanation: decide becomes decision, as in 'to make a decision'.
